articles.title: How does a model learn from examples it was never trained on?
articles.excerpt: Originally published on Medium. Give a language model a few worked examples inside the prompt, and it will do a new task it was never explicitly trained to do. Show it three English sentences translat…
articles.body: Originally published on Medium . Give a language model a few worked examples inside the prompt, and it will do a new task it was never explicitly trained to do. Show it three English sentences translated into French, then an English sentence with no translation, and it produces the French. Show it a few movie reviews labeled positive or negative, then an unlabeled one, and it classifies it. No weights change. No gradient step runs. The model simply reads the examples and adapts, on the spot, in a single forward pass. This is in-context learning, and it is the capability that turned language models from text predictors into general-purpose tools. It is also genuinely strange. Learning, in machine learning, has always meant updating parameters.
articles.author: Adele Chinda

articles.body: A data worth calculator can tell you whether your company's records are in the five-figure, six-figure, or seven-figure conversation — and that is genuinely useful. What it cannot tell you is what your archive will close for. I run DataWorth's valuation guides, and this post is the honest version of how these estimators work, built from a test we keep re-running: five public calculators, one identical company, wildly different answers. The five-calculator test In November 2026 we priced the same hypothetical 100-person company — same headcount, same record families, same history — through five public data-valuation calculators and estimator methods. The outputs spanned $128K to $1M for the identical input profile.

articles.body: JavaScript Error.isError() Is Coming to V8: What the TC39 Proposal Means for Cross-Realm Error Checking This article was written with the assistance of AI, under human supervision and review. The Error.isError() static method checks whether a value is an Error instance using a branded check mechanism that works across realms, addressing silent failures in instanceof Error when errors cross iframe, worker, or Node.js vm module boundaries. The TC39 proposal reached Stage 4 and ships in Chrome 134+, Firefox 138+, and Node.js 23.0+. Problem diagram showing instanceof Error failing with cross-realm error Developers face two distinct failure modes with instanceof Error . An error thrown in an iframe and caught in the parent window returns false because each realm has its own Error constructor.

articles.title: Atom Zero 0.21.0: first behavior-passing adapter and the multi-key wall
articles.excerpt: Atom Zero 0.21.0 is out. This release has a real milestone and a real limit. The copy curriculum now has an adapter that clears the behavior gate on a 250-row mixed held-out set: exact match: 40.0% (t…
articles.body: Atom Zero 0.21.0 is out. This release has a real milestone and a real limit. The milestone: a behavior-passing adapter The copy curriculum now has an adapter that clears the behavior gate on a 250-row mixed held-out set: exact match: 40.0% (threshold 25%) key copy: 54.8% (threshold 40%) key recall: 62.8% content loss: 4.0449 -> 1.0011 full loss: 4.6015 -> 0.9738 gate: pass / promotable It was promoted to a separate curriculum registry, not the product default. Base 0.8.0 remains the only active product model. The chain is now reproducible: staged training -> mixed final eval -> content, exact-match and key-copy gate -> optional promotion -> content-free ledger. The limit: multi-key copying The best adapter is still weak when the prompt contains 2-4 arbitrary keys.

articles.title: Raising the stakes for enterprise networks with AI modernization
articles.excerpt: Enterprise networks are under severe strain. As companies rush to deploy artificial intelligence, the technology is quickly becoming the biggest source of demand on the network. Now, agentic AI is add…
articles.body: Enterprise networks are under severe strain. As companies rush to deploy artificial intelligence, the technology is quickly becoming the biggest source of demand on the network . Now, agentic AI is adding to the load. Tasks conducted by AI agents generate an estimated 450% more network traffic than the same tasks done by human workers. As AI inference shifts from hyperscale training clouds—the huge centralized data centers where raw AI models ingest vast datasets and learn—to real-time, latency-sensitive applications, the need for on-premises or near-premises infrastructure grows. As a result, the gap between enterprise networks that are ready to support AI and those that are not is widening.

articles.title: Double asteroid solar eclipse caught on camera | Space photo of the day for Nov. 24, 2026
articles.excerpt: A spacecraft far from Earth beamed home a rare sight: a solar eclipse caused by one asteroid casting its shadow on another.
articles.body: (Image credit: ESA) A spacecraft far from Earth beamed home a rare sight: a solar eclipse caused by one asteroid casting its shadow on another. What is it? The image shows the Didymos double asteroid system , which consists of the larger Didymos and its moonlet, Dimorphos. In this image, Dimorphos' shadow can be seen on the surface of Didymos. The image was captured by the European Space Agency's (ESA's) Hera probe, which was sent to rendezvous with Didymos. Once there, Hera's job is to inspect the system to study the aftermath of NASA's historic DART mission (Double Asteroid Redirect Test), which slammed a kinetic impactor into Dimorphos in September 2022 in an attempt to alter its orbit and thus the trajectory of the entire two-asteroid system.

articles.body: China will send an international astronaut to its Tiangong space station today (Nov. 24) for the first time ever, and you can watch the landmark liftoff live. A Long March 2F rocket is scheduled to launch the Shenzhou-24 mission from the Jiuquan Satellite Launch Center in northwest China today at 7:18 p.m. EST (0018 GMT and 8:18 a.m. Beijing time on Nov. 25). You can watch the liftoff live here at Space.com, courtesy of China Central Television (CCTV). China rolls out the Long March 2F rocket for its Shenzhou-24 astronaut mission on Nov. 17, 2026. (Image credit: CCTV) Shenzhou-24 will be China's 18th crewed spaceflight to date and its 12th astronaut mission to Tiangong , a three-module station that the nation finished assembling in low Earth orbit in late 2022.
